title: The Foolish Fisherman

full_text:
An impoverished fisherman on the Syrian coast cast his net into the sea and drew up five plump, silver sea-bream, each large enough to feed his family for supper. As he went to place them into his woven basket, a passing sailor remarked jokingly: 'Those are pleasant little fish, brother; but out in the deep water swims the Great Golden Whale, whose scales are worth a king’s ransom!'

The foolish fisherman’s eyes burned with sudden, reckless greed. Looking at his five silver bream with contempt, he said: 'What are five small fish to a man destined to catch a golden whale?'

He threw all five bream back into the foaming waves, pushed his small rowing boat out into the turbulent deep waters, and cast his net in search of the legendary golden whale.

For three days and three nights, beneath burning sun and cold spray, he rowed across the ocean swells. He cast his net a hundred times, but caught only slimy seaweed, jellyfish, and broken driftwood. His water skin went dry, his strength failed, and a sudden storm smashed his oars.

He drifted back to the coast half-dead with hunger and thirst, his boat battered and his hands blistered, without a single fish to bring to his starving children.

Sitting upon the cold sand, the fisherman wept in bitter remorse: 'Cursed be the greed that made me despise five honest fish in pursuit of a phantom whale! A crust of bread in the hand is worth all the golden fish in the deep ocean.'
moral: Do not discard certain, modest sustenance in the vain pursuit of an impossible phantom.
